result:
I’m just going to ramble about how absurdly beautiful the world is when you actually pay attention.

Right now, as I’m typing this, there’s a spider on the ceiling doing that slow, deliberate stalk that looks like it’s moving in 0.25× speed. It’s hunting something I can’t even see, and it’s doing it with eight knees and zero fucks given. Meanwhile, outside my window, a murder of crows is having what sounds like a very heated parliamentary debate about territory or snacks or existential dread. One of them just did a perfect barrel roll for no apparent reason. Absolute theater.

I’ve been thinking lately about how every single thing is on the verge of becoming something else. That spider might die tonight and become crow food by morning. Those crows will eventually become compost. The compost will feed the tree whose leaves will become paper that someone will write a sad poem on. Everything is in the process of eating or being eaten, becoming or unbecoming, and we’re all just temporary arrangements of atoms that learned how to feel melancholy about it.

There’s something wildly comforting in that.

I love how ridiculous humans are. We invented music, then immediately used it to make songs about our exes. We split the atom and also invented the whoopee cushion. We send robots to Mars but still cry at Pixar movies about toys. We’re a glitch in the universe that somehow figured out how to make lasagna and also how to love someone so much it feels like your ribcage is trying to house a second sun.

I don’t know. Maybe the point of all this is just to stay stupidly, stubbornly amazed.

The fact that anything exists at all is statistically offensive. The odds were so bad. And yet here we are—laughing at our own farts, falling in love with people who snore, planting flowers we’ll never live long enough to see fully bloom, writing poems and code and love letters and grocery lists like it matters.

It does matter.

Even the smallest, silliest things matter.

Especially the smallest, silliest things.

Anyway. The spider just caught whatever it was hunting. The crows have moved on to new drama. And I’m sitting here smiling like an idiot because existence is ridiculous and I get to witness it.

Hope you’re having a ridiculous, beautiful day too.
